newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Comalco smelting a loss-maker in 96.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Comalco smelting a loss-maker in 96.

text.p: Bauxite miner and alumina and aluminium producer Comalco Ltd said on Monday its smelting operations operated at a loss in calendar 1996.

Earlier, Comalco reported a A$17.4 million statutory loss for the 1996 year and a joint venture basis net loss of A$16.8 million. Operating profit on a joint venture basis after tax was A$32.9 million, substantially down on the A$264.8 million in 1995.
"The result is unsatisfactory," said Comalco chief executive Terry Palmer in the company's result statement.
"It was unfortunate that the downturn in prices had coincided with the temporary impact on production costs of the extensive smelter upgrade programmes," Comalco said.

"We were hit hard by lower traded metal prices and the strengthening of the Australian dollar at a time when we were implementing the upgrade of the New Zealand smelter and re-starting idled capacity at the Bell Bay smelter," he said.

Palmer said Comalco's share of output was 476,000 tonnes of aluminium in 1996 and will be well over 500,000 tonnes in 1997 given the completion of the upgrade at Tiwai Point and the re-started capacity at Boyne Island.
"We expect the (new line at the) Boyne Island smelter to produce its first metal in May and be fully on-stream by the end of the year," Palmer said.
"We are continuing our investigations into a new alumina refinery and we have plans in place to improve the performance of our Weipa bauxite operations," he said.
The Bell Bay smelter's production capacity is now 138,000 tonnes per year.
Boyne Island produced 260,000 tonnes of metal in 1996.
"However, the smelter's costs were higher than anticipated due to increased prices for fuel, power and coke," Comalco said.
"Negotiations are under way to address these issues," the company said.
Tiwai Point production rose to an annual rate of 313,000 tonnes.
Comalco's shares were down seven cents at A$6.75 at 10.30 a.m. (2330 GMT)
